links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT asthma responses (FRES, FKGL, SMOG) versus recommended patient reading levels
links.effect: Average readability 33.50±14.37 FRES, 12.79±2.89 FKGL, 13.47±2.38 SMOG; all responses difficult and none followed recommended readability levels.
links.quote: However, all responses were of difficult readability, and none followed the recommended readability levels.

links.outcome: Comprehensibility of AI-generated patient information measured by readability scores
links.effect: Mean FRES 33.50±14.37, FKGL 12.79±2.89, SMOG 13.47±2.38; all responses of difficult readability.
links.quote: However, all responses were of difficult readability, and none followed the recommended readability levels.

links.outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT answers to the same question asked twice by different users
links.effect: Only two (6.67%) of the 30 questions had inconsistent answers.
links.quote: Only two (6.67%) of the 30 questions had inconsistent answers.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT's answers to asthma FAQs by physicians for reliability, acceptability, and readability, without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice intervention.
